lesson.title: Triggers and actions: how every Power Automate flow works
body: Every Power Automate flow has the same shape: one trigger, then one or more actions. The trigger is the 'when' (an email arrives, a file is added, it's 9am on Monday). The actions are the 'then' (save the attachment, post in Teams, send an approval).

There are three main kinds of flow. Automated flows start on their own when something happens. Instant flows start when you press a button, in the app or on your phone. Scheduled flows run at set times, like a weekly reminder.

Most problems with flows come from the trigger. If it's too broad (every email, every file), the flow runs far more often than you meant. Add conditions or trigger settings so it only fires for the items you care about, such as emails from one sender or with an attachment.
lesson.takeaway: Before building a flow, finish this sentence: 'When ___ happens, do ___.' The first blank is your trigger; get that right and the rest is easy.

m365.title: Show flagged Outlook emails as tasks in Microsoft To Do
m365.what: Microsoft To Do can pull every email you flag in Outlook into its own 'Flagged email' list, so emails that need action sit alongside your other tasks.
try: Open Microsoft To Do (web, desktop or phone) signed in with the same account as Outlook.
Go to Settings and, under Connected apps, turn on Flagged email.
In Outlook, flag an email that needs a reply or action.
In To Do, open the Flagged email list and add a due date or reminder to it.
When you're done, tick it off in To Do or clear the flag in Outlook; the two stay in step.

explainer.story: Bank of England: 6.5 million mortgages face higher payments
bullets: The Bank's Financial Stability Report (26 Nov) projects about 6.5 million owner-occupier mortgages will see higher payments as fixed deals end between mid-2026 and end-2029, up from about 6 million in July.
The typical rise is around £100 a month, roughly double the July estimate, after Bank Rate went up to 4% on 5 November and gilt yields climbed.
It also flagged risks from heavy AI-related borrowing, and said it will cut capital requirements for major UK banks by about 0.5 percentage points while keeping them 'well capitalised'.
explainer.why: Rising mortgage costs squeeze household budgets well into 2027, on top of January's energy cap rise, and shape what the Bank does with rates on 17 December.

term.meaning: A company that runs cloud computing and data centres at enormous scale, such as Microsoft, Amazon and Google. They are spending heavily on AI data centres, increasingly funded by borrowing.
term.example: The Bank of England says hyperscaler bond issuance is set to top $305bn in 2026, about 8% of global investment-grade bonds.
